issues.symptom: Cova image appears to be a completely different room - lounge/breakroom space vs benchmark bedroom. Ceiling fan, layout, window placement all different. Same 'DAKSH' branding but entirely different architecture

COVABIOPHILIC style poorly expressed. Cova shows industrial/modern elements (black office chair, geometric art blocks) rather than biophilic warmth. Benchmark shows cleaner biophilic elements (pampas grass, botanical art, natural materials)
Orange sofa lacks proper shadow/material definition. Art block swatches on wall appear flat and artificial. Wooden table surface is dull. Benchmark furniture shows superior material authenticity
Sparse, unbalanced composition. Large empty wall space. Office chair relegated to corner. Benchmark shows well-distributed foreground/mid/background elements
Harsh overhead lighting creates unflattering shadows on sofa. Illuminated wall art creates odd lighting inconsistency. Benchmark has warm, directional, cohesive lighting
Orange sofa clashes with cool blue-gray walls. Limited palette. Benchmark demonstrates superior warm/cool balance with cream, natural wood, soft grays
Art blocks appear as flat colored rectangles without texture. Sofa fabric lacks weave detail. Ceiling fan is generic. Benchmark shows sharp, detailed textures throughout
Not magazine-worthy. Harsh lighting, awkward composition, poor color choices. Feels like office breakroom rather than curated interior design. Benchmark is polished and publication-ready
Appears to be a generic lounge space hastily styled, not thoughtfully adapted. Benchmark shows intentional design choices specific to this bedroom's proportions and natural light
Benchmark is significantly superior in every measurable dimension: lighting, composition, style fidelity, photorealism, editorial quality, and overall aesthetic appeal
